reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction by Demis Hassabis from 2014. I ran all three fixed searches and nine more of my own, and opened two pages from 2014. Neither page has him naming a date or length of time for anything AI will do.

- **MIT Technology Review, "Google's Intelligence Designer" (Tom Simonite, 2 December 2014).** This is the only 2014 page I found with his forward-looking words, and it is a news profile with quotes, not a printed Q&A. The nearest thing to a prediction is about DeepMind's technology improving YouTube recommendations and Google's mobile voice search: "You'll see some of our technology embedded into those kinds of things in the next few years." "Next few years" has no date and the line isn't about when AGI arrives, so it fails test 3 and isn't on either list. His other lines there have no timing: AI "will really accelerate progress in solving disease" and "We're still playing Atari games currently… But we are on the first rungs of the ladder."
- **Royal Society Mullard Award announcement (21 November 2014).** His quote is about building up DeepMind and London as a hub for AI research. It contains no AI prediction.

Two other leads didn't work out. The MIT CBMM talk "Towards General Artificial Intelligence" keeps coming up in searches, but its event page calls the Google purchase a past event "in 2014", so the talk was later. I didn't open it. Rory Cellan-Jones's "when hassabis met hawking" post was in the results, but the year it mentions is his own 2014 interview with Stephen Hawking; I didn't open it either.

Searches on the year brought back mostly 2025–26 coverage of his newer timelines ("five to 10 years", "two to three years"). I didn't open those pages, so I've noted them under other_years from headlines only. I meant to run a last search about a WIRED 2014 conference, but it was refused because the 12-search limit had already been reached. I've listed it as not run. I used 2 of the 6 page openings.
